h33-h33-2-b2-RELIEFp10piedmont-20261024-.hypothesis: In Basin-and-Range extensional tectonics, active Quaternary fault scarps concentrate along range-front piedmonts and alluvial fans where strain is accommodated by emergent fault scarps. In contrast, deep basin interiors conceal faults under thick alluvium, and range interiors contain inactive bedrock relics. Shifting 10-15% of dots from low-prior basin and range locations into the piedmont increases the probability of hitting unmapped Quaternary fault traces.
h33-h33-2-b2-RELIEFp10piedmont-20261024-.mechanism: Reallocating mass into the piedmont relief tercile concentrates dot budget where groundwater discharge, break-in-slope, and steep gravity gradients co-occur. Each reallocated dot is placed via greedy exact expected DTI gain on H19-5 ridge support with strong TMI/gravity/scarp expression, ensuring new dots do not cannibalize existing kernel coverage and maintain DTI efficiency.
h33-h33-2-b2-RELIEFp10piedmont-20261024-.non_fault_mimic: Erosional wave-cut shorelines of pluvial lakes (e.g. Lake Lahontan / Lake Bonneville) and alluvial fan regolith boundaries can create break-in-slope and density contrast mimicking piedmont fault scarps without underlying tectonic displacement.
